IDS.name: distributions
IDS.documentation: Distribution function(s) of one or many particle species. This structure is specifically designed to handle non-Maxwellian distribution function generated during heating and current drive, typically solved using a Fokker-Planck calculation perturbed by a heating scheme (e.g. IC, EC, LH, NBI, or alpha heating) and then relaxed by Coloumb collisions.

field.name: ids_properties
field.documentation: Interface Data Structure properties. This element identifies the node above as an IDS

field.name: comment
field.documentation: Any comment describing the content of this IDS

field.name: name
field.documentation: User-defined name for this IDS occurrence

field.name: homogeneous_time
field.documentation: This node must be filled (with 0, 1, or 2) for the IDS to be valid. If 1, the time of this IDS is homogeneous, i.e. the time values for this IDS are stored in the time node just below the root of this IDS. If 0, the time values are stored in the various time fields at lower levels in the tree. In the case only constant or static nodes are filled within the IDS, homogeneous_time must be set to 2

field.documentation: Type of data contained in this occurrence

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: provider
field.documentation: Name of the person in charge of producing this data

field.name: creation_date
field.documentation: Date at which this data has been produced

field.name: version_put
field.documentation: Version of the access layer package used to PUT this IDS

field.documentation: Version of Data Dictionary used to PUT this IDS

field.name: access_layer_language
field.documentation: Programming language of the Access Layer high level API used to PUT this IDS

field.name: node
field.documentation: Set of IDS nodes for which the provenance is given. The provenance information applies to the whole structure below the IDS node. For documenting provenance information for the whole IDS, set the size of this array of structure to 1 and leave the child "path" node empty

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the node within the IDS, following the syntax given in the link below. If empty, means the provenance information applies to the whole IDS.

field.name: reference
field.documentation: List of references used to populate or calculate this node, identified as explained below. In case the node is the result of of a calculation / data processing, the reference is an input to the process described in the "code" structure at the root of the IDS. The reference can be an IDS (identified by a URI or a persitent identifier, see syntax in the link below) or non-IDS data imported directly from an non-IMAS database (identified by the command used to import the reference, or the persistent identifier of the data reference). Often data are obtained by a chain of processes, however only the last process input are recorded here. The full chain of provenance has then to be reconstructed recursively from the provenance information contained in the data references.

field.name: timestamp
field.documentation: Date and time (UTC) at which the reference was created, expressed in a human readable form (ISO 8601) : the format of the string shall be : YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Example : 2020-07-24T14:19:00Z

field.name: distribution
field.documentation: Set of distribution functions. Every distribution function has to be associated with only one particle species, specified in distri_vec/species/, but there could be multiple distribution function for each species. In this case, the fast particle populations should be superposed

field.name: wave
field.documentation: List all waves affecting the distribution, identified as in waves/coherent_wave(i)/identifier in the waves IDS

field.name: type
field.documentation: Wave/antenna type. index=1 for name=EC; index=2 for name=IC; index=3 for name=LH

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: antenna_name
field.documentation: Name of the antenna that launches this wave. Corresponds to the name specified in antennas/ec(i)/name, or antennas/ic(i)/name or antennas/lh(i)/name (depends of antenna/wave type) in the ANTENNAS IDS.

field.name: index_in_antenna
field.documentation: Index of the wave (starts at 1), separating different waves generated from a single antenna.

field.name: process
field.documentation: List all processes (NBI units, fusion reactions, ...) affecting the distribution, identified as in distribution_sources/source(i)/process in the DISTRIBUTION_SOURCES IDS

field.name: type
field.documentation: Process type. index=1 for NBI; index=2 for nuclear reaction (reaction unspecified); index=3 for nuclear reaction: T(d,n)4He [D+T->He4+n]; index=4 for nuclear reaction: He3(d,p)4He [He3+D->He4+p]; index=5 for nuclear reaction: D(d,p)T [D+D->T+p]; index=6 for nuclear reaction: D(d,n)3He [D+D->He3+n]; index=7 for runaway processes

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: reactant_energy
field.documentation: For nuclear reaction source, energy of the reactants. index = 0 for a sum over all energies; index = 1 for thermal-thermal; index = 2 for beam-beam; index = 3 for beam-thermal

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: nbi_energy
field.documentation: For NBI source, energy of the accelerated species considered. index = 0 for a sum over all energies; index = 1 for full energiy; index = 2 for half energy; index = 3 for third energy

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: nbi_unit
field.documentation: Index of the NBI unit considered. Refers to the "unit" array of the NBI IDS. 0 means sum over all NBI units.

field.name: nbi_beamlets_group
field.documentation: Index of the NBI beamlets group considered. Refers to the "unit/beamlets_group" array of the NBI IDS. 0 means sum over all beamlets groups.

field.name: gyro_type
field.documentation: Defines how to interpret the spatial coordinates: 1 = given at the actual particle birth point; 2 =given at the gyro centre of the birth point

field.name: type
field.documentation: Species type. index=1 for electron; index=2 for ion species in a single/average state (refer to ion structure); index=3 for ion species in a particular state (refer to ion/state structure); index=4 for neutral species in a single/average state (refer to neutral structure); index=5 for neutral species in a particular state (refer to neutral/state structure); index=6 for neutron; index=7 for photon

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: ion
field.documentation: Description of the ion or neutral species, used if type/index = 2 or 3

field.name: element
field.documentation: List of elements forming the atom or molecule

field.name: atoms_n
field.documentation: Number of atoms of this element in the molecule

field.name: z_ion
field.documentation: Ion charge (of the dominant ionization state; lumped ions are allowed)

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying ion (e.g. H+, D+, T+, He+2, C+, ...)

field.name: state
field.documentation: Quantities related to the different states of the species (ionization, energy, excitation, ...)

field.name: z_min
field.documentation: Minimum Z of the charge state bundle (z_min = z_max = 0 for a neutral)

field.name: z_max
field.documentation: Maximum Z of the charge state bundle (equal to z_min if no bundle)

field.name: name
field.documentation: String identifying ion state (e.g. C+, C+2 , C+3, C+4, C+5, C+6, ...)

field.name: electron_configuration
field.documentation: Configuration of atomic orbitals of this state, e.g. 1s2-2s1

field.name: vibrational_mode
field.documentation: Vibrational mode of this state, e.g. "A_g". Need to define, or adopt a standard nomenclature.

field.name: neutral
field.documentation: Description of the neutral species, used if type/index = 4 or 5

field.documentation: List of elements forming the atom or molecule

field.name: neutral_type
field.documentation: Neutral type, in terms of energy. ID =1: cold; 2: thermal; 3: fast; 4: NBI

field.documentation: Number of particles in the distribution, i.e. the volume integral of the density (note: this is the number of real particles and not markers)

field.name: particles_fast_n

field.documentation: Total energy of the fast particles in the distribution

field.name: energy_fast_parallel
field.documentation: Parallel energy of the fast particles in the distribution

field.name: torque_tor_j_radial
field.documentation: Toroidal torque due to radial currents

field.name: current_phi
field.documentation: Toroidal current driven by the distribution

field.name: power_first_orbit
field.documentation: Power loss due to first orbit losses

field.name: power_rotation
field.documentation: Power going to plasma rotation. This power goes into sustaining the plasma rotation rather than heating the plasma. This is given because the injection energy in the rotating plasma frame is (assuming rotation in the same direction of the NB injection) lower than in the lab-frame.

field.name: power_charge_exchange
field.documentation: Power loss due to Charge Exchange loss of fast ions

field.name: collisions
field.documentation: Power and torque exchanged between the species described by the distribution and the different plasma species through collisions

field.name: thermalization
field.documentation: Volume integrated source of thermal particles, momentum and energy due to thermalization. Here thermalization refers to non-thermal particles, sufficiently assimilated to the thermal background to be re-categorized as thermal particles. Note that this source may also be negative if thermal particles are being accelerated such that they form a distinct non-thermal contribution, e.g. due run-away of RF interactions.

field.documentation: Source rate of thermal particles due to the thermalization of fast particles

field.documentation: Power input to the thermal particle population due to the thermalization of fast particles

field.name: torque
field.documentation: Torque input to the thermal particle population due to the thermalization of fast particles

field.documentation: Identifier of the wave or particle source process, defined respectively in distribution/wave or distribution/process

field.name: type
field.documentation: Type of the source term. Index = 1 for a wave, index = 2 for a particle source process

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: torque_phi
field.documentation: Total toroidal torque of the source

field.name: profiles_1d
field.documentation: Radial profiles (flux surface averaged quantities) for various time slices

field.name: rho_tor_norm
field.documentation: Normalized toroidal flux coordinate. The normalizing value for rho_tor_norm, is the toroidal flux coordinate at the equilibrium boundary (LCFS or 99.x % of the LCFS in case of a fixed boundary equilibium calculation, see time_slice/boundary/b_flux_pol_norm in the equilibrium IDS)

field.name: rho_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal flux coordinate = sqrt(phi/(pi*b0)), where the toroidal magnetic field, b0, corresponds to that stored in vacuum_toroidal_field/b0 and pi can be found in the IMAS constants

field.name: psi
field.documentation: Poloidal magnetic flux. Integral of magnetic field passing through a contour defined by the intersection of a flux surface passing through the point of interest and a Z=constant plane. If the integration surface is flat, the surface normal vector is in the increasing vertical coordinate direction, Z, namely upwards.

field.name: volume
field.documentation: Volume enclosed inside the magnetic surface

field.name: area
field.documentation: Cross-sectional area of the flux surface

field.name: surface
field.documentation: Surface area of the toroidal flux surface

field.name: psi_magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: psi_boundary
field.documentation: Value of the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary (useful to normalize the psi array values when the radial grid doesn't go from the magnetic axis to the plasma boundary)

field.name: is_delta_f
field.documentation: If is_delta_f=1, then the distribution represents the deviation from a Maxwellian; is_delta_f=0, then the distribution represents all particles, i.e. the full-f solution

field.name: ggd
field.documentation: Distribution represented using the ggd, for various time slices

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: path
field.documentation: Path of the grid, including the IDS name, in case of implicit reference to a grid_ggd node described in another IDS. To be filled only if the grid is not described explicitly in this grid_ggd structure. Example syntax: #wall:2/description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, means that the grid is located in the wall IDS, occurrence 2, with relative path description_ggd(1)/grid_ggd, using Fortran index convention (here : first index of the array)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: geometry_type
field.documentation: Type of space geometry (0: standard, 1:Fourier, >1: Fourier with periodicity)

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: coordinates_type
field.documentation: Type of coordinates describing the physical space, for every coordinate of the space. The size of this node therefore defines the dimension of the space.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: objects_per_dimension
field.documentation: Definition of the space objects for every dimension (from one to the dimension of the highest-dimensional objects). The index correspond to 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes, .... For every index, a collection of objects of that dimension is described.

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects for a given dimension

field.name: boundary
field.documentation: Set of (n-1)-dimensional objects defining the boundary of this n-dimensional object

field.name: neighbours
field.documentation: List of indices of the n-dimensional objects adjacent to the given n-dimensional object. An object can possibly have multiple neighbours on a boundary

field.name: geometry
field.documentation: Geometry data associated with the object, its detailed content is defined by ../../geometry_content. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered.

field.name: nodes
field.documentation: List of nodes forming this object (indices to objects_per_dimension(1)%object(:) in Fortran notation)

field.name: measure
field.documentation: Measure of the space object, i.e. physical size (length for 1d, area for 2d, volume for 3d objects,...)

field.name: geometry_2d
field.documentation: 2D geometry data associated with the object. Its dimension depends on the type of object, geometry and coordinate considered. Typically, the first dimension represents the object coordinates, while the second dimension would represent the values of the various degrees of freedom of the finite element attached to the object.

field.name: geometry_content
field.documentation: Content of the ../object/geometry node for this dimension

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Space dimension of the grid subset elements, using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: element
field.documentation: Set of elements defining the grid subset. An element is defined by a combination of objects from potentially all spaces

field.name: object
field.documentation: Set of objects defining the element

field.name: space
field.documentation: Index of the space from which that object is taken

field.name: dimension
field.documentation: Dimension of the object - using the convention 1=nodes, 2=edges, 3=faces, 4=cells/volumes

field.name: base
field.documentation: Set of bases for the grid subset. For each base, the structure describes the projection of the base vectors on the canonical frame of the grid.

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: metric
field.documentation: Metric of the canonical frame onto Cartesian coordinates

field.name: tensor_covariant
field.documentation: Covariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: tensor_contravariant
field.documentation: Contravariant metric tensor, given on each element of the subgrid (first dimension)

field.name: temperature
field.documentation: Reference temperature profile used to define the local thermal energy and the thermal velocity (for normalization of the grid coordinates)

field.name: orbit_frequency_pol
field.documentation: Poloidal orbit frequency (transit or bounce) at the grid location (in phase space)

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.name: orbit_frequency_tor
field.documentation: Toroidal orbit frequency (transit or precession) at the grid location (in phase space)

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.name: expansion
field.documentation: Distribution function expanded into a vector of successive approximations. The first element in the vector (expansion(1)) is the zeroth order distribution function, while the K:th element in the vector (expansion(K)) is the K:th correction, such that the total distribution function is a sum over all elements in the expansion vector.

field.name: grid_subset
field.documentation: Values of the distribution function expansion, for various grid subsets

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.name: expansion_fd3v
field.documentation: Distribution function multiplied by the volume of the local velocity cell d3v, expanded into a vector of successive approximations. The first element in the vector (expansion(1)) is the zeroth order distribution function, while the K:th element in the vector (expansion(K)) is the K:th correction, such that the total distribution function is a sum over all elements in the expansion vector.

field.name: grid_subset
field.documentation: Values of the distribution function expansion, for various grid subsets

field.name: grid_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid used to represent this quantity

field.name: grid_subset_index
field.documentation: Index of the grid subset the data is provided on. Corresponds to the index used in the grid subset definition: grid_subset(:)/identifier/index

field.name: values
field.documentation: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.

field.name: coefficients
field.documentation: Interpolation coefficients, to be used for a high precision evaluation of the physical quantity with finite elements, provided per element in the grid subset (first dimension).

field.name: amplitude
field.documentation: Value of the distribution function at the grid position in phase space. The interpolation coefficients refer to a C-2 spline.

field.name: orbit
field.documentation: Orbit description of the particle at this position in phase space. First dimension is the element index. Second dimension is the time along the orbit. Third dimension contains the particle phase space coordinates.

Second dimension: first matrix index. Third dimension: second matrix index. Fourth dimension: coefficient index

field.name: values

field.name: markers
field.documentation: Distribution represented by a set of markers (test particles)

field.name: coordinate_identifier
field.documentation: Set of coordinate identifiers, coordinates on which the markers are represented

field.name: index
field.documentation: Integer identifier (enumeration index within a list). Private identifier values must be indicated by a negative index.

field.name: weights
field.documentation: Weight of the markers, i.e. number of real particles represented by each marker. The dimension of the vector correspond to the number of markers

field.name: positions
field.documentation: Position of the markers in the set of coordinates. The first dimension corresponds to the number of markers, the second dimension to the set of coordinates

field.name: orbit_integrals
field.documentation: Integrals along the markers orbit. These dimensionless expressions are of the form: (1/tau) integral (f(n_tor,m_pol,k,eq,...) dt) from time - tau to time, where tau is the transit/trapping time of the marker and f() a dimensionless function (phase factor,drift,etc) of the equilibrium (e.g. q) and perturbation (Fourier harmonics n_tor,m_pol and bounce harmonic k) along the particles orbits. In fact the integrals are taken during the last orbit of each marker at the time value of the time node below

field.name: expressions
field.documentation: List of the expressions f(n_tor,m_pol,k,q,...) used in the orbit integrals

field.name: n_phi
field.documentation: Array of toroidal mode numbers, where quantities vary as exp(i.n_phi.phi) and phi runs anticlockwise when viewed from above

field.name: m_pol
field.documentation: Array of poloidal mode numbers, where quantities vary as exp(-i.m_pol.theta) and theta is the angle defined by the choice of ../../coordinate_identifier, with its centre at the magnetic axis recalled at the root of this IDS

field.name: orbit_integrals_instant
field.documentation: Integrals/quantities along the markers orbit. These dimensionless expressions are of the form: (1/tau) integral ( f(eq) dt) from time - tau to time_orbit for different values of time_orbit in the interval from time - tau to time, where tau is the transit/trapping time of the marker and f(eq) a dimensionless function (phase, drift,q,etc) of the equilibrium along the markers orbits. The integrals are taken during the last orbit of each marker at the time value of the time node below

field.name: expressions
field.documentation: List of the expressions f(eq) used in the orbit integrals

field.name: time_orbit
field.documentation: Time array along the markers last orbit

field.name: toroidal_mode
field.documentation: In case the orbit integrals are calculated for a given MHD perturbation, index of the toroidal mode considered. Refers to the time_slice/toroidal_mode array of the MHD_LINEAR IDS in which this perturbation is described

field.name: vacuum_toroidal_field
field.documentation: Characteristics of the vacuum toroidal field (used in rho_tor definition and in the normalization of current densities)

field.name: r0
field.documentation: Reference major radius where the vacuum toroidal magnetic field is given (usually a fixed position such as the middle of the vessel at the equatorial midplane)

field.name: b0
field.documentation: Vacuum toroidal field at R0 [T]; Positive sign means anti-clockwise when viewing from above. The product R0B0 must be consistent with the b_tor_vacuum_r field of the tf IDS.

field.name: magnetic_axis
field.documentation: Magnetic axis position (used to define a poloidal angle for the 2D profiles)
